name: Question 18
problem:
Find the gradient of the product $g(x,y)h(x,y),$ given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}g(x,y) & ={e}^{x-y},\, &  & ∇g(x,y)={e}^{x-y}\,i-{e}^{x-y}\,j, &  &  \\ h(x,y) & ={x}^{2}-3xy,\, &  & ∇h(x,y)=(2x-3y)\,i-3x\,j. &  & \end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $g(x,y)$ and $h(x,y)$ is given by

$$
∇[gh]=h∇g+g∇h.
$$

Using the product rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[g(x,y)h(x,y)] & =h(x,y)∇g(x,y)+g(x,y)∇h(x,y) \\  & =({x}^{2}-3xy)({e}^{x-y}\,i-{e}^{x-y}\,j)+{e}^{x-y}((2x-3y)\,i-3x\,j) \\  & =(({x}^{2}-3xy){e}^{x-y}\,i-({x}^{2}-3xy){e}^{x-y}\,j)+((2x-3y){e}^{x-y}\,i-3x{e}^{x-y}\,j) \\  & ={e}^{x-y}({x}^{2}-3xy+2x-3y)\,i-{e}^{x-y}({x}^{2}-3xy+3x)\,j \\  & ={e}^{x-y}(({x}^{2}-3xy+2x-3y)\,i-({x}^{2}-3xy+3x)\,j).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 18

Find the gradient of the product g(x,y)h(x,y), given that g(x,y)=ex−y,∇g(x,y)=ex−yi−ex−yj,h(x,y)=x2−3xy,∇h(x,y)=(2x−3y)i−3xj.

a
 ex−y((x2−3xy)i−3xj)
b
 ex−y((x2−3xy+2x−3y)i−(x2−3xy+3x)j)
c
 ex−y((2x−3y)i−3xj)
d
 ex−y((x2−3xy−2x−3y)i+(x2+3xy+3x)j)
e
 ex−y((x2−3xy−y)i+(x2+3xy+3x)j)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The gradient of the product of two functions g(x,y) and h(x,y) is given by ∇[gh]=h∇g+g∇h.

Using the product rule, we obtain ∇[g(x,y)h(x,y)]=h(x,y)∇g(x,y)+g(x,y)∇h(x,y)=(x2−3xy)(ex−yi−ex−yj)+ex−y((2x−3y)i−3xj)=((x2−3xy)ex−yi−(x2−3xy)ex−yj)+((2x−3y)ex−yi−3xex−yj)=ex−y(x2−3xy+2x−3y)i−ex−y(x2−3xy+3x)j=ex−y((x2−3xy+2x−3y)i−(x2−3xy+3x)j).
